title: Lockout/tagout awareness
summary: Awareness of hazardous energy control for everyone who works around machines and plant: what lockout/tagout is, why you never remove someone else's lock, and what to do when you find equipment locked out. Authorized employees also need your site's full procedure and practical training.
tags: lockout, tagout, energy isolation, industrial, starter
overview: A starter course written by Resgrid in plain language for affected employees. It does not authorize anyone to apply locks. Your site's energy control procedure and the occupational safety rules where you operate come first.

lessons.title: Why equipment is locked out
lessons.html: Machines and plant store energy: electrical, mechanical, hydraulic, pneumatic, chemical and thermal. Before anyone services or repairs them, that energy is isolated and locked so that the equipment cannot start or release it.

lessons.title: When you find a lock or a tag
lessons.html:
• Never remove, bypass or operate equipment that carries someone else's lock or tag.
  • Never try to start locked-out equipment to check it.
  • Ask the person named on the tag or your supervisor when you need the equipment back.
